findings.evidence: template/scripts/finish_task.py:954-971 (new helper) and :1060-1082 (original block). Both call queue_local_status, then sync_merged_task with the same SystemExit messages. The existing test had to change its side_effect from [None, waiting] to [None, None, waiting] to cope with the extra read.
findings.summary: The new sync_queue_merged_task helper copies the existing queue-observation and merged-sync block further down in main(). Finish now reads the queue PR state twice and calls sync_merged_task twice on the merged path. The second call is idempotent, but it costs an extra PR read and leaves two copies of the same error-handling logic to keep in step.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/finish_task.py:1049 calls sync_queue_merged_task before managed_candidate(work). The orphan and provenance checks follow at :1053-1054. The added tests cover only candidate=True.
findings.summary: The early sync now runs for every coordinator-mode PR finish, not only for managed candidates. It fast-forwards the worktree before require_no_orphan_active_openspec and require_delivery_provenance run. A merged non-candidate task is therefore synchronized before the gates that previously preceded it. This looks harmless, but it is an untested ordering change.
